In a joint status report filing, Apple states it has not received a response from Jon Prosser's attorneys in a month, with his legal representation explaining that Prosser is busy caring for a newborn. Details below.

Prosser's discovery process repeatedly delayed

Last year, shortly after unveiling iOS 26, Apple sued Prosser over a video leaking the "Liquid Glass" redesign.

Apple accused Prosser, alongside Michael Ramacciotti, of misappropriating trade secrets and violating the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act by accessing the contents of an Apple employee's development iPhone and publishing leaks based on them.

According to multiple court filings submitted since, Ramacciotti promptly complied with Apple's discovery requests, while Prosser did not formally respond to the lawsuit. Prosser has since denied the allegations.

As a result, the court granted Apple's motion for a default judgment against Prosser, essentially meaning he can no longer contest Apple's claims unless the ruling is set aside.

Last June, Prosser's legal team moved to set aside the default judgment, arguing this would be the most efficient way to advance the case. The court granted the motion, opening a first round of discovery in which Prosser provided Apple with documents and communications and sat for a deposition.

However, in a joint status report filed yesterday, Apple says progress has since been limited, with its legal team citing the leaker's second child having just been born.

The filing reads:

Apple and Mr. Prosser have endeavored to advance this matter through limited discovery. Mr. Prosser provided documents and communications to Apple and sat for a deposition on June 16, 2026. Unfortunately, despite multiple attempts by Apple to contact and follow up regarding outstanding discovery, the most recent response from Mr. Prosser's counsel was received on July 6, 2026. The documents Mr. Prosser has produced appear to remain deficient, and Apple has raised these issues with Mr. Prosser's counsel. Shortly before this joint status report was filed, Mr. Prosser's counsel explained that the delay in responding may be attributable to Mr. Prosser having just welcomed his second child and being occupied with caring for a newborn. Mr. Prosser's counsel indicated that a date will be scheduled to provide further discovery to Apple.

The report, signed by counsel for Apple, Ramacciotti, and Prosser, also notes that Ramacciotti has agreed to supplement his interrogatory responses and will sit for a second deposition in September, with the parties expecting to file another status report on October 7.
